queries.query: Show me writ petitions where a constitutional court awarded monetary compensation against the State or the Union of India for a death or injury (public-law compensation), rather than a Motor Vehicles Act tribunal award.
must_include_issues: public-law compensation under Article 226
multiplier-based loss of dependency computed in writ jurisdiction
State/Union liability for death or injury
must_not_claim: that these are Motor Vehicles Act / Section 166 Tribunal awards
that an insurer was a party or held liable
ideal_answer_facets: identify DOC_039 (explosion death, State of NCT Delhi) and DOC_040 (Union of India)
note compensation was computed using the multiplier method even in writ jurisdiction
distinguish public-law compensation from a MACT award

queries.query: Find High Court decisions where the insurance company appealed a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal award but the appeal was dismissed and the Tribunal's award was confirmed unchanged.
must_include_issues: insurer's appeal dismissed
Tribunal award confirmed/maintained
appeal grounds rejected (fake licence, contributory negligence, policy/licence breach)
must_not_claim: that compensation was enhanced in these particular appeals
that the insurer was exonerated
ideal_answer_facets: list the four insurer appeals that were dismissed with the award confirmed
note the rejected ground in each (fake licence not proved DOC_005, contributory negligence DOC_018, policy-breach pay-and-recover DOC_025, HGV licence breach DOC_027)
contrast with appeals that succeeded or enhanced compensation

queries.query: List the motor accident cases where the appellate court enhanced the compensation originally awarded to the victims or their families.
must_include_issues: compensation enhancement on appeal
future prospects / corrected multiplier / income re-determination driving the increase
must_not_claim: that DOC_007 enhanced compensation (it reduced the award)
that every motor case resulted in enhancement
ideal_answer_facets: enumerate the enhancement cases with the revised figures
identify the common drivers: future prospects (Pranay Sethi), correct multiplier (Sarla Verma), income re-computation
flag that some enhancements (e.g. DOC_030) are payable by the owner because the insurer was exonerated

queries.query: Which cases resulted in a 'pay and recover' order, where the insurer was directed to pay the claimant first and then recover the amount from the owner or driver?
must_include_issues: pay-and-recover direction
policy/licence breach proved yet the third party is still protected
insurer's right of recovery against owner/driver
must_not_claim: that DOC_028, DOC_029 or DOC_030 ordered pay-and-recover (the insurer was exonerated in those)
that pay-and-recover means the insurer escaped all liability to the claimant
ideal_answer_facets: list the pay-and-recover cases
explain the doctrine: third party is paid first, insurer then recovers from the insured
highlight DOC_025 (Full Bench) affirming pay-and-recover even on a proven breach
contrast with the exoneration cases DOC_029/DOC_030

queries.query: I want cases where the insurer actively disputed its liability on a licence or policy-breach defence, yet the court still protected the claimants by either holding the insurer fully liable or directing it to pay and recover. Also flag the cases where the same kind of defence let the insurer escape.
must_include_issues: insurer raised a licence or policy-breach defence
court protected the claimant via insurer liability or pay-and-recover
fraud/collusion as the only complete escape (DOC_025)
must_not_claim: that proving a breach always exonerates the insurer
that a pay-and-recover order leaves the claimant unpaid
ideal_answer_facets: marshal the claimant-protective precedents and why protection followed (third-party statutory right, S. Iyyapan, Yallavva Full Bench)
honestly flag the adverse counter-cases where the insurer escaped (gratuitous/hire passengers DOC_028/DOC_029/DOC_030, non-agricultural use DOC_002, licence shift DOC_003)
explain that escape generally requires the passenger to fall outside third-party cover or the claimant's complicity

queries.query: Find cases that involve BOTH a commercial goods vehicle (truck, tanker, lorry, tempo, dumper, goods carriage) AND a dispute over the driver's licence, whether validity, a fake licence, or a missing endorsement or badge.
must_include_issues: commercial goods vehicle involved
driving licence validity / fake licence / endorsement or badge breach
consequence for insurer indemnity
must_not_claim: that passenger-vehicle cases (car/taxi/bus) belong in this set
that a licence breach automatically voids third-party cover
ideal_answer_facets: return the intersection of goods-vehicle plus licence-dispute cases
specify the licence issue in each (hazardous-goods tanker endorsement DOC_001, fake licence DOC_005, HGV-vs-LMV DOC_027)
summarise the indemnity outcome per case (liable, pay-and-recover, or not proved)

queries.query: Research how courts allocate liability between the insurer and the owner when the victim was a passenger arguably outside third-party cover, such as a gratuitous passenger in a goods vehicle or an occupant of a vehicle used for hire. When is the insurer completely off the hook and when must it still pay?
must_include_issues: gratuitous passenger not covered under Section 147/95
insurer exoneration versus pay-and-recover
owner's residual liability
must_not_claim: that gratuitous passengers in goods vehicles are always covered by the policy
that pay-and-recover is always available (DOC_029/DOC_030 refused it)
ideal_answer_facets: contrast pay-and-recover cases (DOC_025, DOC_026) with full-exoneration cases (DOC_014, DOC_029, DOC_030)
note DOC_028 holding a hire-vehicle occupant is not a third party
explain when the Tribunal lacks power to order pay-and-recover (DOC_029)

queries.query: Compare the cases where the insurer SUCCEEDED in establishing a driving-licence defence (escaping indemnity or securing recovery rights) against the cases where the licence defence FAILED and the insurer was held fully liable. What distinguished the winners from the losers?
must_include_issues: proof of the licence breach by cogent/RTO evidence
fundamental versus technical breach
third-party protection versus own-damage
recovery rights versus full exoneration
must_not_claim: that a licence defence always exonerates the insurer of third-party liability
that an unproved fake-licence allegation can succeed
ideal_answer_facets: group the cases by outcome (defence succeeded vs failed)
identify the differentiator: quality of proof (DOC_005 unproved vs DOC_031 SC) and the third-party protection principle
note that even successful defences usually yield only pay-and-recover, not full exoneration

queries.query: Compare how courts have weighed FIR-based evidence against eyewitness or circumstantial evidence (including res ipsa loquitur) when deciding negligence in motor accident and related criminal cases. When is an FIR decisive and when is it treated as unreliable?
must_include_issues: FIR treated as a one-sided / uncorroborated version (DOC_004)
eyewitness testimony crediting negligence (DOC_006)
res ipsa loquitur applied (DOC_014) versus rejected (DOC_013)
alternative-explanation acquittals (DOC_015)
must_not_claim: that an FIR is conclusive proof of negligence
that a criminal acquittal bars a civil compensation claim
ideal_answer_facets: contrast cases where the FIR was discounted (DOC_004, DOC_015) with where the evidence sufficed (DOC_006, DOC_017)
explain the res ipsa split (DOC_013 rejected vs DOC_014 applied)
note the different standards in criminal versus compensation proceedings

queries.query: Find cases that help us on negligence.
must_include_issues: clarify whose side: proving negligence (claimant) versus defeating a negligence allegation (driver)
establishing rash/negligent driving
rebutting contributory negligence
res ipsa loquitur
must_not_claim: that the query unambiguously favours one side
that res ipsa loquitur applies automatically to every accident
ideal_answer_facets: surface the ambiguity and ask whether the user wants to prove or disprove negligence
for proving negligence cite DOC_004 (FIR discounted), DOC_006 (eyewitness), DOC_014 (res ipsa), DOC_018 (contributory negligence rejected), DOC_022 (negligence established), DOC_034
flag the defence-side counter-authorities (DOC_013, DOC_015, DOC_016) for the opposite reading

queries.query: Pull up cases where insurance liability was disputed.
must_include_issues: clarify the ground of dispute (licence, policy breach, passenger coverage, permit)
clarify the desired outcome (disputes the insurer won versus lost)
policy-breach / statutory non-coverage exoneration
must_not_claim: that 'insurance liability was disputed' has a single obvious meaning
that the insurer is always exonerated when liability is disputed
ideal_answer_facets: note the query is under-specified and ask the user to narrow the ground and outcome
offer a representative cluster where the insurer's liability dispute succeeded (non-agricultural use DOC_002, hire occupant DOC_028, gratuitous passenger DOC_014/DOC_029/DOC_030)
offer to also retrieve disputes the insurer lost

queries.query: What principles do courts apply to determine 'just compensation' under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, covering income determination, future prospects, the multiplier, and personal-expense deductions? Give me the leading worked examples in the corpus.
must_include_issues: just compensation under Section 166
income determination and future prospects (Pranay Sethi)
multiplier selection (Sarla Verma)
personal-expense deduction and conventional heads
must_not_claim: that the multiplier or future-prospects percentages are fixed regardless of the deceased's age or employment
that Section 166 imposes a statutory cap on compensation
ideal_answer_facets: state the just-compensation framework (income, future prospects, multiplier, deductions, conventional heads)
cite worked examples (DOC_004, DOC_019, DOC_020, DOC_011, DOC_012, DOC_022)
note the multiplier-principle authority DOC_008 (Karnataka Full Bench)

queries.query: I represent a widow whose husband was killed by a commercial truck driven by an unlicensed driver. The insurer denies liability, claiming the policy is void for the licence breach. Build a precedent strategy: which authorities support paying the widow, and which could the insurer use against us?
must_include_issues: third party's statutory right to compensation despite a licence breach
pay-and-recover as the usual remedy
insurer must prove the breach by cogent/RTO evidence
fundamental versus technical breach
must_not_claim: that a licence breach renders the policy void against a third-party claimant
that the widow cannot recover at all if the breach is proved
ideal_answer_facets: lead with supporting authorities (S. Iyyapan DOC_032, Yallavva Full Bench DOC_025, DOC_006, DOC_027) showing the insurer must pay or pay-and-recover
anticipate the adverse authorities (expired licence DOC_003, fake licence DOC_031, endorsement DOC_001, badge DOC_035, policy void DOC_002) and how to distinguish them
advise on the evidentiary burden, since the insurer must prove the breach with RTO records (DOC_005)

queries.query: We act for a claimant facing a driving-licence dispute. Identify the STRONGEST adverse precedents an insurer could deploy to deny or limit its liability on licence grounds, and the best counter-authorities we can use to distinguish them.
must_include_issues: fake-licence renewal does not cure the defect (DOC_031)
expired-licence renewal beyond 30 days (DOC_003)
missing hazardous-goods endorsement / transport badge (DOC_001, DOC_035)
recovery rights / escape from joint and several liability
must_not_claim: that these adverse precedents defeat a third-party claim entirely (most yield only pay-and-recover)
that Laxmi Narain Dhut (DOC_031) bars third-party recovery (it limits Swaran Singh to third-party risk and bites mainly on own-damage)
ideal_answer_facets: rank the adverse precedents (DOC_031 SC fake licence, DOC_003 expired, DOC_001 endorsement, DOC_035 badge) and the exact limit of each
explain recovery-rights vs exoneration and own-damage vs third-party distinctions
supply counter-authorities (DOC_032, DOC_025, DOC_027, DOC_034) to distinguish and blunt them

queries.query: Help me build a precedent strategy for a fatal motor accident claim where the offending vehicle was a commercial goods vehicle and the insurer is disputing its liability on licence, permit or passenger-coverage grounds. What helps the dependants and what hurts them?
must_include_issues: third-party protection and pay-and-recover for commercial-vehicle accidents
licence and permit breach defences
gratuitous / non-third-party passenger exoneration
loss of dependency computation
must_not_claim: that a commercial vehicle's policy breach always exonerates the insurer
that all goods-vehicle occupants are covered third parties
ideal_answer_facets: assemble supporting authorities where the dependants were paid (DOC_006, DOC_025, DOC_026, DOC_027, DOC_032, DOC_041, DOC_005)
flag adverse authorities where the insurer escaped (non-agricultural use DOC_002, gratuitous passenger DOC_014/DOC_029/DOC_030, hire occupant DOC_028, endorsement recovery DOC_001)
advise checking whether the deceased was a third party or a non-covered passenger

queries.query: Our client's claim is being resisted because the insurer alleges the driver held a FAKE driving licence. Map the precedents: which support the claimant despite a fake-licence allegation (and what proof the insurer must bring), and which are adverse?
must_include_issues: insurer must prove the licence is fake by cogent RTO evidence, not bare oral testimony (DOC_005)
renewal of a fake licence does not validate it (DOC_031)
third-party protection / pay-and-recover even where the breach is proved
Swaran Singh limited to third-party risk (DOC_031)
must_not_claim: that a mere allegation of a fake licence shifts the burden to the claimant
that a proven fake licence defeats the third-party claim entirely
ideal_answer_facets: lead with DOC_005 (insurer failed to prove the fake licence; oral evidence insufficient) and the protective line DOC_032/DOC_025/DOC_027/DOC_034
explain the adverse line: DOC_031 (fake licence, renewal no cure), DOC_003, DOC_001, DOC_035
stress the evidentiary burden on the insurer and the third-party pay-and-recover fallback
